learningOutcomes: Understand the basic steps involved in starting and running a market stall.
Identify suitable products or services to sell and understand the target customer.
Research markets, pitches, stall fees and local trading opportunities.
Calculate basic costs, prices, revenue and potential profit.
Create an attractive, accessible and professional stall layout.
Communicate confidently with customers and develop basic selling skills.
Understand different payment methods and basic cash-handling procedures.
Keep simple records of sales, costs, stock and income.
Identify key permissions, insurance, consumer, safety and trading considerations relevant to the stall.
Understand how to promote a market stall using local networks and social media.
Respond appropriately to common problems such as poor weather, low sales, difficult customers or stock shortages.
Create a practical action plan for launching their own market stall.
shortDescription: Learn how to plan, set up and run a market stall, from choosing what to sell and pricing your products to attracting customers, taking payments and understanding your basic responsibilities.
fullDescription:
This practical course introduces learners to the essential skills needed to start and successfully run a market stall.

It is designed for beginners, including people considering self-employment, testing a small business idea, selling handmade or second-hand goods, promoting a community project, or earning additional income.

Learners will work through the complete market-stall journey: developing an idea, researching local opportunities, calculating costs, setting prices, preparing stock, presenting a professional stall, communicating confidently with customers, taking payments and keeping basic records.

The course will also introduce important practical considerations such as permissions, insurance, consumer responsibilities, food-related requirements where applicable, health and safety, security and managing money.

Activities should encourage learners to apply the course directly to their own idea. By the end, each learner should have developed a simple plan for their own market stall that they could continue developing in the real world.

Where examples are used, they should be relevant to Ely, Cardiff and surrounding communities, while teaching skills that can be applied elsewhere.
title: How to Run a Successful Market Stall

learningOutcomes: Explain how the reputation of a local community is created and how it can change over time.
Identify positive assets within Ely, including people, community groups, businesses, services, spaces, activities and local achievements.
Recognise the difference between positive community promotion and ignoring or hiding genuine community problems.
shortDescription: Learn practical ways to promote Ely positively, celebrate local strengths, challenge unfair stereotypes and become a confident ambassador for your community.
title: Promoting Our Local Area: Building a Positive Reputation for Ely
fullDescription:
Every community has a story. The way that story is told can influence how residents feel about where they live, how outsiders view the area, whether people want to visit or invest, and how local businesses, organisations and community projects develop.

This course is designed for people who live, work, volunteer or participate in the community of Ely, Cardiff and want to help build a stronger and more positive reputation for the area.

Learners will explore how community reputation is created through everyday conversations, social media, local events, businesses, community organisations, photographs, videos, news stories and the experiences people share with others.

The course does not ignore challenges within the community. Instead, learners will explore how to talk about local problems constructively while also recognising Ely's people, achievements, businesses, organisations, history, culture, opportunities and community strengths.

Learners will develop practical communication and community-promotion skills that can be used online and offline. Activities will encourage learners to identify positive stories, discover overlooked community assets, create promotional content and think about how their own behaviour contributes to Ely's reputation.

The course will also explore responsible social-media use, responding constructively to negative comments, avoiding misinformation, celebrating community achievements and encouraging other residents to participate positively.

By the end of the course, learners should understand that promoting an area is not simply advertising it. It is about helping create a community that people are proud to belong to and ensuring that its strengths, achievements and potential are visible to others.
